sentences.text: 9. It is the case of the appellant that now he stands convicted and sentenced to undergo rigorous imprisonment for ten years besides fine of Rs. 10,000/- and in default thereof, an additional rigorous imprisonment for one year, appeal has been admitted, he has remained in custody for six years and six months, the appeal is not likely to be taken up, he may be extended bail.
10. Learned APP opposes the prayer submitting that after proper trial, he stands convicted though he concedes that the appeal is not likely to be taken up in near future.
11. Considering the submissions of the parties, the appeal has been admitted, the appellant is in custody right from the date of occurrence continuously till he has been convicted.

As per the learned counsel for the appellant, he has no criminal antecedent, the appeal is not likely to be taken up in near future, solely taking into account his continuous jail custody period for more than six years,
this Court is inclined to grant him relief.

Let the appellant, namely, SHEKHAR SAHANI, be released on bail on furnishing bail bond of Rs. 10,000/- with two sureties of the like amount each to the satisfaction of learned 1st Additional Session Judge-cum-Special Judge, POCSO Act, Muzaffarpur in connection with Trial No. 62/2018 arising out of Ahiyapur P.S Case No. 443/2018, subject to the following conditions:-
(i) one of the bailors should be the family members/relative of the appellant who shall provide official document to show his bona fide;
(ii) the appellant shall desist from committing any criminal offence again, failing which the State shall be at liberty to take steps for cancellation of his bail bonds.
